messages:
Maria: FYI customer reported sudden cross-region routing — requests from EU app are landing in us-west -> massive latency + 429 spike and unexpected billing. Ticket #C-8761 attached.
Ian: copying in net/infra. Do we have a recent push to DNS prefetch/prefill?
Ash: not a deploy but we did roll a geodb refresh 8h ago. Could be a split-brain between prefill cache and live DB.
Customer: our users in Frankfurt see median p95 go from 80ms to 1.3s and lots of 429s since 09:12 UTC. We only see origin ineu endpoints in config.
Ben: can you paste a sample request id + headers? need x-rc, x-edge-pop, x-resolver-ip if present.
Customer: request-id=rr-0a1b2c3d header dump: x-edge-pop: iad1, x-resolver-ip: 185.22.10.5, x-rc: 429. Happened across multiple ISPs.
Ian: that resolver-ip is European but returning US pop answers -> likely ISP resolver cache returning stale prefetch answer. Could be ECS strip/EDNS issue.
Ash: please run a quick dig from their resolver and from a public resolver. Ask the customer to run:
```
dig +short @185.22.10.5 example.redwood.ai A
dig +short @8.8.8.8 example.redwood.ai A
```
Customer: ran it, output: from 185.22.10.5 => 18.200.1.10 (us-west); from 8.8.8.8 => 3.120.30.5 (eu-west).
Kai: aha. So ISP resolver is returning stale cached answer. But why would it prefer us-west? check prefetch TTLs and our CNAME rotation window.
Ben: can you also share our edge logs for rr-0a1b2c3d?
deploy-bot: deploy:geodb-refresh v2026-03-17-08:04 rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T08:04Z
Ash: that geodb refresh lined up with our prefill flush job. I'm seeing a window where old prefill answers lingered in some resolver cohorts (split-brain).
Maria: customer asks for repro steps so they can mitigate on their side (clear resolver caches if possible).
Ian: repro steps for us: 1) simulate resolver with stale cache by answering A->us-west for customer name; 2) hit our auth endpoint and observe 429s where we expect eu tokens to be validated against eu auth cluster -> requests forwarded to us-west which has different auth cookie shard.
Ben: example curl to reproduce (from an EU client):
```
curl -i -H "Host: example.redwood.ai" --resolve example.redwood.ai:443:18.200.1.10 https://example.redwood.ai/api/v1/predict -d '{"input":"x"}'
```
Ian: expected: route to eu cluster, actual: lands in us-west and auth fails -> 401/429 fallback cascade.
Ash: mitigation options: - advise customer to set short client DNS TTL/disable local resolver caching (if possible) - we can publish an emergency cname TTL clamp and a prefill invalidation.
Kai: operationally we can: 1) roll back geodb refresh to previous version for affected regions, 2) force prefill re-seed with prefer-eu answers, 3) add temporal stickiness to resolver affinity to prefer region by origin IP. All carry tradeoffs.
Maria: customer needs a hotfix timeline. Can infra estimate time to rollback?
Kai: rollback of geodb to previous snapshot: ~25m, prefill re-seed: ~10m, invalidation propagation depends on upstream ISPs (could be minutes to hours). We can push emergency route to prefer-eu for their customer prefix specifically (if they provide resolver IP ranges).
Ben: created short runbook here -> steps executed: rollback geodb, trigger prefill-seed, monitor edges for x-edge-pop flip.
Ian: also add quick telemetry check: query count from resolver cohorts returning non-eu answers in last hour (`resolver_cohort != eu AND answer_pop == us-west`).
Maria: Customer: can you share a small sample of resolver IPs (5) that show the us-west answer so we can target?
Customer: shared 5 IPs in ticket: 185.22.10.5, 185.22.10.9, 185.22.11.2, 92.208.15.1, 92.208.15.3
Ash: running a targeted invalidation for those cohorts now.
deploy-bot: job:prefill-invalidate started for cohorts [185.22.10.0/24,92.208.15.0/24]
Ben: monitor shows x-edge-pop switching back to eu in ~3 minutes for 3/5 IPs, remaining two still return us-west.
Ian: ETA on rollback?
Kai: starting rollback now, will update in ~20m.
Maria: customer: we'll keep you posted and can credit overcharged tokens due to the spike. Sorry for the disruption. :heart:
Customer: appreciated, please ping when resolved.
Ben: rollback completed, prefill re-seed finished, targeted invalidation done. Observed resolver cohort flip to eu for all 5 IPs after second pass.
Ash: postmortem notes: race between geodb refresh and prefill invalidation created a short split-brain where some ISP resolvers answered stale IPs. Root cause: prefill invalidation order + TTL window.
Ian: follow-ups: add a prefill-safe ordering (invalidate caches after geodb fully propagated), add a breaker to delay geodb canary promotion if prefill seed lag > X, and expose a resolver cohort map to support for rapid targeting.
Maria: creating escalation ticket for SLA/billing credit and linking runbook + suggested fixes.
Customer: confirmed resolution, latency back to normal. Thanks. :thumbsup:
